policy.principle: Claude Opus is THE teacher (gold labels, hard reasoning, judge). Open Qwen is comparator + bulk_labeler + inspector — not a teacher rival. Verifiers (tests/executors/contract checkers) are the strictest teacher of all because they produce objective truth.
policy.kael_moat: Kael competes on integration depth × speed × cost — NOT on benchmark parity with Opus. A 7-14B model will not match Opus on hard reasoning, and trying to is the wrong target. Kael wins by knowing GAD's planning surface cold, by emitting clean tool-actions, by escalating to Opus only when needed, and by being an order of magnitude faster + cheaper.
policy.fallback_chain: primary_teacher → fallback_teacher (Sonnet when Opus rate-limited) → bulk_labeler (Haiku for cheap volume; Qwen-Coder-32B for offline) → comparator (open-weight reproducibility row) → verifier (tests, always)

policies.rationale: Opus emits cleaner Python with fewer hallucinated APIs; tests provide objective truth.
Opus follows error traces and reproduces failure cases best; verifier is the project's actual test suite.
Tool-action emission rarely needs Opus-tier reasoning; Sonnet emits clean JSON cheaply. Schema validators are the truth.
Opus + R1 distill are the two strongest math reasoners we can route to.
Multi-step game/agent trajectories need Opus's planning depth; Kael learns from corrected trajectories. Note Anthropic-output IP review required before training (per Kael-house scoping report).
Paraphrase quality is fungible; Haiku is the best cost/quality tradeoff. Augmentation requires variance per memory project_augmentation_requires_variance.md.
CoT trace quality is a teacher capability; Opus emits the strongest reasoning traces, R1-distill provides open-weight comparator.
Cross-vendor judge panel: Opus + GPT-5 + Gemini disagreement signal flags ambiguous rows. Per slm-learning-103 frontier comparator row.
Inspection requires open weights; closed APIs cannot expose hidden states. Same-family with Kael backbone preferred.
